description: Soloft Industries, yazılım, yapay zekâ, veri bilimi ve ileri mühendislik alanlarında yenilikçi çözümler geliştiren bir teknoloji girişimidir. NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 kapsamında, NASA’nın Dünya gözlem verilerini kullanarak tarımsal risklerin analizini ve sürdürülebilir tarım uygulamalarını destekleyen veri odaklı çözümler geliştirmeyi hedefliyoruz. Teknoloji ve mühendisliği gerçek dünya problemleriyle buluşturarak ölçülebilir etki yaratmayı amaçlıyoruz.
summary: Zira is a decision-support platform for dryland farmers, agronomists and cooperatives. On sowing-decision day it shows how many millimetres of plant-available water a field's soil holds, with an uncertainty range, and compares three rotations (current, water-triggered flexible, legume-based) over 24 seasons of NASA data. It reads each field's cropped-or-fallow history from Landsat 8/9 and MODIS NDVI, runs a daily FAO-56 water balance on NASA POWER weather, and cross-checks the model with SMAP, GPM IMERG and GRACE-FO. A soil-moisture sensor, simulated in this version, can correct the model. The result becomes a printable Zira Card and a short WhatsApp message that reaches the farmer only after an agronomist approves it. Zira addresses Field Shift by replacing calendar-based planning (such as "wheat, then fallow") with water-based evidence in the Konya Closed Basin, Türkiye, where groundwater falls and over 740 sinkholes are recorded. Zira does not decide; it helps the farmer and agronomist decide with evidence.
details: What it does. Zira answers one question: "How much usable water does this field hold on sowing day, and which rotation does that water carry?" An agronomist draws a field on a map. Zira then (1) fetches 25 years of NASA POWER weather, (2) reads ten seasons of NDVI from inside the field polygon, from Landsat 8/9 at 30 m with MODIS as fallback, and calls each season cropped, fallow or unknown for the agronomist to confirm, (3) runs a daily FAO-56 water balance (Penman–Monteith ET0, crop coefficients, root-zone storage) with a low–mid–high range, and (4) replays three rotations on identical weather, soil and starting water. A season counts as "water was enough" if actual divided by potential evapotranspiration is at least 0.70.
